blocks.value: Sometimes one or more candlesticks form patterns that help traders understand market sentiment. These are called candlestick patterns.
Imagine This: Farmers often look at dark clouds to guess whether it might rain. The clouds don't guarantee rain, but they provide clues. Candlestick patterns work in a similar way.
Some popular patterns include Doji, Hammer, Shooting Star, Bullish Engulfing and Bearish Engulfing. These patterns indicate possible changes in buying or selling pressure.
⚠️ No candlestick pattern guarantees that a stock will move in a particular direction. They provide probabilities, not certainty.
A Hammer appearing after a sharp fall may suggest that buyers are becoming stronger, but it should always be confirmed using other information.
Never make investment decisions using only one candlestick pattern.
